_comment: The judge's limits and calibration, stated once; every size, endpoint, key name and judge-specific threshold is read from here (judge_profile.py for Python, src/judge-profile.ts for Node, which apply the same rules). SUPERJEV_JUDGE picks the profile (default below; 'fake' is the test judge and uses the default's numbers). kind names the implementation that speaks to it. key_env is the environment variable holding its API key. aliases are other accepted names. window_tokens is the judge's hard input ceiling for the state plus the longest question; bytes_per_token is the one size rule (judge tokens = UTF-8 bytes / this, rounded up, high on purpose); input_cap_headroom is the room left under the window for the question battery, call_headroom how far one call's budget sits under the input cap; max_questions_per_call is how many questions one call may carry; input_usd_per_mtok is its published input price per million tokens; max_parts is how many judge calls one direct check may need before it is refused; file_ceiling_bytes is the largest file that connects whole; gate_window_tokens is the evidence window the Stop gate sends; overloaded_statuses are the HTTP codes that mean try again, retried retry_attempts times starting retry_first_delay_ms apart (doubling); too_big_status is the code that means the request was over the window. The calibration numbers are measured for one judge and must be re-measured for another: confidence_line (under it a human reads the source), sure_line, confirm_floor, source_floor, claim_content_floor, route_floor, preflight_strong (ask.py), outcome_line and max_confidence_above_peak (the organizer/outcome accept gate; Node reads both).

typesafe-jev._source: window: the measured hard input ceiling; questions: the per-call cap every batcher plans under; price: docs.typesafe.ai, checked 2026-09-16
